points.description: Pandas and koalas are similar because both are specialists: each eats almost exclusively one food (pandas eat almost only bamboo; koalas eat almost only eucalyptus leaves), so they depend on stable, specific environments/niches.

levels.says: Says both are specialists or have restricted diets, but does not give the bamboo/eucalyptus evidence.

points.description: Both differ from pythons because pythons are generalists that can adapt to and thrive in many environments/foods (e.g. living in the Everglades, eating alligators, rats; spreading to new climates) and do well amid change/near humans, unlike specialists.

levels.says: Says pythons are different or adaptable, with no support from the article or no link to specialists vs generalists.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both: pandas and koalas are specialists with narrow diets (bamboo, eucalyptus), and pythons are adaptable generalists. Equivalent wording is accepted. Half marks are for a correct idea with no article support. The invasive-species prompt is not covered, since the total is 2 marks for the koala/panda item.
